headline: Funding flows. Supply chains stress. Data bottlenecks loom.
deck: This week, investors are placing bets while supply chain vulnerabilities become glaringly apparent.

stories.head: True Anomaly raises $190M at $1.6B valuation
stories.body: True Anomaly secured $190M in a Series C funding round, bringing its valuation to $1.6B. This capital will bolster its co-orbital security and space domain awareness capabilities, tapping into rising DoD demand. With a growing focus on national security, this funding round underscores the shift towards space-based defense solutions.
stories.soWhat: The cash flow in this sector is impressive, but it raises questions about how much innovation is genuinely happening versus just financial maneuvering.

stories.head: U.S. space supply chains depend on China
stories.body: A recent report highlights the heavy dependence of U.S. space supply chains on Chinese manufacturing. This reliance is likened to trusting your ex for a ride, underscoring the risks involved. With geopolitical tensions rising, this could become a critical vulnerability for U.S. aerospace firms.
stories.soWhat: If the chips fall the wrong way, we might see a scramble for domestic alternatives that could disrupt timelines and budgets.

stories.head: Cardinality wall threatens LEO satellite operations
stories.body: The satellite industry is facing a 'cardinality wall' as thousands of spacecraft crowd low Earth orbit, leading to potential data bottlenecks. This issue could hinder operational efficiency for companies like SpaceX and OneWeb, who are racing to deploy their constellations. As the congestion increases, the industry must innovate to manage the growing data demands.
stories.soWhat: More satellites might mean less data utility, which is a paradox that could trip up even the most ambitious launch schedules.

watchlist.title: Keep an eye on Starfighters' microgravity testing
watchlist.body: Starfighters Space's pivot to microgravity flight testing could attract new contracts from NASA, making it a player in commercial parabolic capabilities.

watchlist.title: Monitor Palantir's TITAN program extension
watchlist.body: Palantir's $480M extension on the TITAN program suggests continued government investment in ground station capabilities, which may lead to more lucrative contracts.

watchlist.title: Watch for updates on hypersonic testing delays
watchlist.body: The ongoing delays in hypersonic glide-vehicle tests could impact defense spending and timelines, forcing a reevaluation of priorities in the sector.

watchlist.title: Track Sierra Space's Dream Chaser progress
watchlist.body: With the Dream Chaser DoD variant passing its design review, its eventual launch could shift logistics strategies for military operations in space.

talent.statLabel: Week-over-week growth in resumes from primes to Series B/C
talent.head: Talent is leaving big-aero — and it's not about money
talent.body: Compensation is not the gating factor. The complaint, almost universally, is schedule risk — the inability to ship anything quickly, the half-decade gap between joining and seeing flight hardware, the meeting that exists to schedule the meeting. The startups absorbing this talent will, in two years, be hard to compete with on a level playing field.
